Classify eDISH peak quadrants and concurrent Hy's Law

Source: R/classify_hyslaw.R
classify_hyslaw.Rd

Peak eDISH uses each subject's on-treatment maximum ALT or AST / ULN versus maximum bilirubin / ULN (not necessarily the same day). Concurrent (biochemical potential) Hy's Law requires bilirubin meeting bili_cut on or after an ALT/AST meeting alt_cut, within window_days. ALP meeting alp_cut in the same window can optionally exclude the subject from potential Hy's Law.

Usage

classify_hyslaw(
  adsl = NULL,
  adlb = NULL,
  prepped = NULL,
  window_days = 14,
  alt_cut = 3,
  bili_cut = 2,
  alp_cut = 2,
  exclude_alp = TRUE,
  compare = c(">=", ">"),
  ...
)

Arguments

adsl

ADSL-like data. Ignored when prepped is supplied.

adlb

ADLB-like data. Ignored when prepped is supplied.

prepped

Optional list from prep_hyslaw_data().

window_days

Concurrent window in days after the ALT/AST elevation. Default 14 matches the pharmaverse admiral Hy's Law vignette.

alt_cut

ALT/AST ULN multiple.

bili_cut

Bilirubin ULN multiple.

alp_cut

ALP ULN multiple used for cholestasis exclusion and the cholestatic screening plot.

exclude_alp

If TRUE, concurrent cases with ALP meeting alp_cut in the window are not counted as potential Hy's Law.

compare

">=" (default) or ">". FDA / many CSR shells use strict greater-than; this package defaults to greater-or-equal.

...

Passed to prep_hyslaw_data() when prepped is NULL.

Value

The prepped list with a subject-level subjects data frame.

Details

Baseline records are kept for mDISH (peak / baseline) ratios. They are not used as eDISH maxima.
